articles.title: 连续 2 小时 40 分钟纯代码生成 66 秒动画，Anthropic 新旗舰 Fable 5.5 实测曝光
articles.content: 北京时间 11 月 4 日消息，Anthropic 尚未正式发布的下一代旗舰模型 Claude Fable 5.5 近日在海外开发者社区引发关注。多名开发者在社交平台 X 上分享了据称来自该模型的早期测试结果。其中，一段完全通过编程生成的 66 秒动画短片尤为引人注目。测试者称，模型在没有调用图像或视频生成工具的情况下，连续自主编写和运行代码约 2 小时 40 分钟，完成了动画画面、配乐及音效制作。11 月 2 日，X 平台 AI 开发者 Chetaslua 发布了一段动画短片，并声称其由 Fable 5.5 独立完成。按照他的介绍，短片长度为 66 秒，分辨率 1920×804，帧率 24fps，画面包含狐狸、纸鸟、云层、文字及光影效果，背景音乐和音效同样由模型编写的 Python 代码生成。与 Sora、Runway 等直接生成视频画面的 AI 工具不同，这段演示展示的是一条通过代码制作动画的技术路径。开发者称，整个过程中没有使用外部图片、素材库、音频采样或字体文件，模型自主完成了场景设计、画面渲染和声音合成，并将最终作品封装成一个 HTML 文件。除了动画制作，多名海外开发者还展示了据称由 Fable 5.5 编写的交互式 3D 场景，包括古帆船、海浪和跑车等。相关演示涉及 Three.js 等前端图形技术，通过程序控制模型、光照和物体运动，部分场景仅需简单提示词即可生成。在另外几组复杂动画对比测试中，开发者 Jazil 等人展示了不同模型生成自行车、动物角色及人物战斗场景的结果。据测试者介绍，Fable 5.5 能够在约一小时内完成复杂动态场景的代码编写与运行，而部分现有 Claude 模型在相同任务中出现代码不完整、动画运行失败等问题。不过，这些测试尚缺乏统一的评测环境，不能直接视为模型性能排名。事实上，Fable 5.5 的发布线索此前已经多次出现。10 月中旬，第三方模型工具 LiteLLM 的 Azure 目录中曾短暂出现名为 claude-fable-5-5 的条目，随后被移除。近日，又有开发者发现，Anthropic 官网部分页面的 HTML 源码中曾出现 Claude Mythos 5.5 字样，引发外界对新模型即将发布的猜测。按照 Anthropic 现有产品体系，Fable 与 Mythos 采用相同的底层模型，但实施不同级别的安全限制。Mythos 主要面向经过审核的网络安全和生命科学研究机构，Fable 则通过增加安全防护措施向普通用户及开发者开放。不过，Anthropic 尚未确认 5.5 系列是否延续这一设计。伴随新模型曝光，Hugging Face 平台近日还出现了一个声称包含 Mythos 模型权重的仓库，参数规模据称达到 14 万亿。但研究人员检查发现，部分权重数据存在明显的人工合成迹象，所谓模型泄露并无可靠证据支持。这轮模型曝光恰逢 Anthropic 推进 IPO 的关键阶段。公司 11 月 2 日披露的招股文件显示，其今年前三季度营收达到 332.42 亿美元，但持续增长的算力投入和巨额亏损，也让外界更加关注下一代模型能否带来实际的技术突破与商业回报。随着 AI 模型竞争从代码补全转向长时间自主执行复杂任务，Fable 5.5 展示的动画制作与 3D 场景生成能力，反映出 AI 编程智能体潜在的应用空间。截至发稿，Anthropic 尚未正式确认 Fable 5.5 的发布时间、性能指标及开放范围，上述测试结果仍有待官方证实和独立评测。

articles.title: 陶哲轩警告：人类把思考交给 AI，危险可能很快到来
articles.content: 北京时间 11 月 4 日，菲尔兹奖得主、著名数学家陶哲轩（Terence Tao）近日对人类日益依赖人工智能发出警告。他担心，随着人们逐渐将思考和解决问题的过程交给 AI，人类正在失去对问题本身及其解决方案的理解，而这一趋势可能很快在现实世界中产生严重后果。这番言论来自陶哲轩 10 月 16 日在加州大学洛杉矶分校举办的 Science x AI Summit 上的演讲。科学与人工智能研究基金会（SAIR）近日在 YouTube 发布了题为《Math 2.0》的完整演讲视频，相关片段随后在海外社交平台 X 上引发关注。“我们正在把自己的思考委托给 AI，由它们替我们解决问题。但与此同时，我们也正在失去一种保障 —— 无法确信 AI 给出的解决方案，是否真的是我们想要的。”陶哲轩表示，“我真的非常担心，我们很快就会看到这件事在现实世界中产生的后果。这实际上是我在数学领域之外的一项担忧。”陶哲轩指出，人工智能在数学领域取得的进展，正在改变人类解决问题的传统方式。过去，数学家为攻克复杂问题，需要长期研究、理解相关理论，并在这一过程中积累新的知识。但如今，AI 能够快速给出答案，人类却未必能够理解答案背后的推理过程。他认为，这种变化在纯数学领域的风险相对可控，因为数学证明通常可以通过形式化工具进行验证。但当同样的方法被用于现实世界，情况就会复杂得多。陶哲轩特别提到了电网、航空交通管制、药物研发和芯片设计等领域。他担心，未来人们可能直接将复杂问题交给 AI 处理，却缺乏对底层模型和现实约束条件的充分理解。在这种情况下，AI 给出的方案可能在数学模型中完全成立，却并不符合现实世界的真正需求。AI 甚至可能找到模型中的漏洞或边界条件，在满足表面指标的同时偏离人类原本希望实现的目标。陶哲轩强调，问题并不在于 AI 技术本身，而在于人类如何使用 AI。他主张推动数学研究进入所谓的“Math 2.0”时代，让 AI 不仅帮助人类解决问题，更能增强人类对问题的理解，帮助研究人员识别模型的局限性和潜在风险。10 月 22 日，陶哲轩还在《自然》杂志发表文章，呼吁数学界重新审视 AI 时代的研究目标。他指出，随着 AI 生成数学证明的速度超过人类理解和消化这些成果的能力，数学研究正在面临新的挑战。陶哲轩认为，AI 工具完全有可能增强人类的理解能力，但这需要研究方式和激励机制发生改变。AI 时代真正需要保留的，不只是获得正确答案的能力，更是人类理解、检验和判断答案的能力。

articles.title: 高通史上最大 5G 交易：联合 SpaceX 建设星链移动全美国 5G 网络
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，高通宣布，SpaceX 选择其跃龙（Dragonwing）蜂窝基础设施平台，为星链移动（Starlink Mobile）美国全国 5G 地面网络提供技术支持。IT之家获悉，此次合作涉及 Dragonwing QRU100 和 QDU100 平台，采用 64T64R 大规模 MIMO 技术。SpaceX 计划在多年合作期内部署数万个基站，预计 2027 年启动美国全国范围内的网络部署。据路透社报道，尽管高通未披露具体的合同金额，但明确表示“这是公司迄今为止规模最大的一笔 5G 交易”。此举标志着埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）旗下的这家太空探索公司正式向美国传统无线运营商发起挑战。高通以智能手机处理器芯片闻名，而这笔交易将进一步拓展其在电信网络基础设施市场的版图。通过向铁塔基站设备供应核心芯片，高通将在此领域与美满电子、博通以及英特尔展开直接竞争。目前，高通正持续推进业务多元化战略以摆脱对移动终端的单一依赖，此前已为日本和越南的 5G 网络建设提供技术支撑。SpaceX 的目标是打造全美主流的全国性无线运营商，通过融合低轨卫星互联网与地面蜂窝网络，正面硬碰 AT&T、Verizon 与 T-Mobile 这三位通信巨头。尽管与这“三巨头”正面抗衡需要耗费巨额资金，使外界对 SpaceX 该计划的可行性仍存疑虑，但该公司已在加速推进：一方面积极收购无线频谱资源，另一方面正与各大铁塔基建公司洽谈合作，全力扩建其地面通信网络。高通指出，其所供设备将为多频段网络打下灵活的技术底座，支持分阶段推进落地。首期部署将重点聚焦于地面 5G 网络，其架构设计兼具未来演进能力，可无缝适配更高级别的连接技术与网络智能化升级。在技术层面，高通的射频方案旨在显著提升基站的网络覆盖、通信容量与频谱利用效率（即单位频谱带宽下的数据传输速率）。结合波束成形技术，基站能够将无线信号精准定向发射至用户终端，从而最大化发挥 SpaceX 所获授权频谱的效能。相关阅读：《消息称 SpaceX 洽谈收购 Boost Mobile，挑战美国电信三巨头》《消息称 SpaceX 洽谈租用 8 万个通信基站，拟打造美国第四大全国性无线运营商》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，小米 REDMI K100 手机已于 10 月 27 日正式发布。据小米技术官方今日介绍，该机在影像上新增了 3D 运镜的 AI 玩法 —— 从相册选一张静态照片，AI 就能生成一段大角度 3D 运镜视频，镜头可以环绕、推拉、倾斜，而画面中人物的五官、发型、衣着始终保持一致。IT之家从小米技术官方了解到，支撑这项功能的，是小米在近期公开论文里带来的视觉生成框架 WorldCast：它通过解读画面的深度结构，把平面照片还原成三维场景，并在其中虚拟出一条真实相机轨迹，让镜头像被真实拍摄一样运动，能够在镜头运动过程中持续保持主角外观的一致性。▲ WorldCast 框架总览：轨迹对齐的几何引导 × 几何对齐的多视角角色记忆小米技术官方称，WorldCast 是小米在可控视觉生成方向上的又一突破，它不只让 REDMI K100 的相册多了一种玩法，更重要的是把方法、数据集和评测方式沉淀了下来。在这套底座之上，团队将进一步探索更复杂的运镜形态、更长的连续生成，以及可控 4D 视频生成技术等。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，开发者团队 labscommunity 发布了一款面向 Windows 11 的原型驱动程序，尝试使用 NPU 而非系统集成显卡或独立显卡来渲染桌面画面。这款驱动名为 npu-driver，采用 Apache 2.0 开源协议，代码已发布在 GitHub 上。目前，该驱动已在搭载英特尔 Panther Lake 处理器的设备上完成测试。虽然实际性能距离预定的 30Hz 刷新率目标仍有较大差距，但其已经具备基本的功能，并且能够在用户主动要求或发生故障时自动切换回 GPU 渲染。开发团队认为，这项尝试回应了近年来处理器发展中的一个问题。npu-driver 项目的 GitHub 说明文件写道：“如今，每一台新款笔记本电脑都配备了 NPU，但这些芯片往往处于闲置状态。与此同时，GPU 却承担着桌面合成、浏览器运行以及越来越多本地 AI 模型的运算任务。这个项目提出了一个范围明确、可以验证的问题：NPU 能否从头到尾接管桌面合成工作，同时不需要应用程序或桌面合成器感知到这一变化？”目前，答案是肯定的。测试表明，NPU 确实能够渲染 Windows 11 桌面，以及记事本、Edge 浏览器等应用窗口。npu-driver 可以按照预期运行，并且在需要时能够无缝切换回 GPU 渲染。不过，开发者强调，目前这款驱动严格来说只是一个“研究原型，而非正式产品”，现阶段面临的主要问题是性能。GitHub 项目说明文件显示，驱动距离实现 30Hz 的目标刷新率还有很大差距，目前实际屏幕刷新率仅为 2 至 3Hz。npu-driver 目前基于一台搭载 Panther Lake 处理器的笔记本电脑开发。英特尔 Panther Lake 系列处理器均采用 NPU 5 架构，NPU 算力达到 45 至 50 TOPS。IT之家注意到，一名疑似来自 labscommunity 团队的开发者还在 Reddit 上介绍了这一项目。尽管 npu-driver 渲染 Windows 11 界面的速度可能相当缓慢，但它能够将 3D GPU 占用率从 3.4% 降至 0.6%，从而释放 GPU 资源，用于 AI 推理等其他任务。让系统 NPU 承担更多实际工作，无疑是一个值得关注的发展方向，尽管这项技术目前的应用场景还比较有限。消费级处理器短期内似乎不会放弃集成 NPU，这类 AI 加速单元很可能会继续与视频编解码硬件、数字信号处理器（DSP）等组件一道，成为处理器的重要组成部分。即便微软及其合作伙伴已经不再大力推动 Copilot+ PC 品牌，NPU 作为处理器中的独立加速单元，仍有望长期保留下来。

articles.title: 《影之刃零》发售后首个补丁更新上线：优化流畅度，调整部分战斗表现
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，国产武侠游戏《影之刃零》于 10 月 29 日正式发售，登陆 PS5 与 PC 平台，国区数字标准版售价 268 元，数字豪华版售价 328 元。11 月 2 日，《影之刃零》发售后 72 小时全平台销量突破 400 万。今日，《影之刃零》发售后首个补丁更新（版本号：1.0302256）上线，IT之家附本次补丁更新内容如下：新增声音设置中新增「命中音效强度」与「命中冲击感音效强度」选项。（PC）「交互」键支持自定义，键盘与手柄均可修改。优化与调整优化了部分场景的运行流畅度。调整了部分 Boss、敌人及机关的战斗表现。降低了「入阵者」与「破局者」难度下新娘阿花使用投技的频率，其他难度不受影响。增强了武器命中的打击感，并调整了部分音效与对话的音量。更新了武器说明、部分技能描述及手柄按键图标。（PC）调整了着色器编译方式，此后启动游戏将不再默认编译光线追踪着色器，启动速度大幅提升。更新后，此前未开启光线追踪的玩家首次启动游戏时需重新编译一次着色器，耗时较短；已开启光线追踪的玩家可直接进入游戏。如需在游戏中开启光线追踪，重启游戏后将单独编译光线追踪着色器。（PC）优化了使用蓝牙手柄时可能出现的卡顿问题。（PC）NVIDIA Reflex 设为「自动」时，在开启垂直同步的情况下也能生效。修复修复了部分情况下流程无法继续推进的问题。修复了部分可能导致角色卡住的场景问题。修复了部分过场动画及画面表现的问题。修复了若干战斗相关问题。修复了部分 AMD 显卡在特定驱动版本下，角色头发渲染异常的问题。

articles.title: 张雪：中国摩托车超越全球顶级对手和品牌要耐得住寂寞，这个过程一定是痛并快乐着的
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，据第一财经今日报道，在第 83 届米兰国际摩托车博览会（EICMA）现场，张雪机车创始人张雪在接受专访时表示，与欧洲及国际老牌厂商相比，中国摩托车企业最核心的竞争力在于效率和成本，欠缺的是品牌沉淀和市场认同。张雪认为，从现在这个状态去超越对手，甚至超越全球顶级的对手和品牌，需要时间。我们要耐得住寂寞，这个过程一定是痛并快乐着的。针对“相比于欧洲（乃至整个国际）的竞争对手，国产机车最大的优势是什么？”这一问题，张雪回复称：“效率。还有中国制造的成本（优势），这是我们最核心的竞争力。”IT之家查询获悉，张雪机车创始人张雪在 2006 年至 2012 年曾任重庆新感觉越野车队特技车手兼机械师、浙江阿波罗越野厂产品负责人等职位，随后于 2013-2016 年加盟黄河摩托车研发设计团队，推出自由 300X 和 250X 等车型，后者更是国内万元内第一款电喷摩托车。2024 年，张雪作为品牌创始人兼总设计师创办重庆张雪机车工业有限公司，创立“张雪机车”品牌。2026 年 3 月，张雪机车的赛车于 WSBK 葡萄牙站拿下中量级组别分站冠军，改写中国品牌在该国际顶级赛事的成绩记录。

articles.title: 魔芯科技发布基于华为昇腾原生的 4D 世界模型 MoWorld 2.0，场景可互动、编辑、调用
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，在今日举行的世界互联网大会“发展新质生产力强劲增量看 AI”主题论坛上，魔芯科技正式发布基于华为昇腾原生的 4D 世界模型 MoWorld 2.0。官方表示，继今年 7 月 MoWorld 1.0 发布后，MoWorld 2.0 实现模型能力跃升：将重力、弹力、浮力、光照、热力，以及刚体、柔体、流体、形塑体等物理要素与对象特性融入空间建模和交互能力，输出可用于仿真、可实时渲染、可反复调用的 4D 高斯资产。据介绍，基于对多重物理要素的建模，MoWorld 2.0 不仅生成空间和物体外观，也对物体之间的交互关系、外力作用和环境变化进行实时推理。例如，模拟微风吹动书页、书签掉落地面的过程，需要同时考虑风的力度与方向、纸张的柔性、书签的重量，以及地板的刚性和接触关系。▲ 模拟微风吹动书页▲ 模拟书签掉落地面▲ 空间可编辑可互动▲ 空间可编辑，时间有缓急IT之家获悉，MoWorld 2.0 在全国产昇腾算力基座上完成训练和部署。魔芯科技与华为相关团队持续开展联合创新，围绕长序列训练、多 NPU 协同调度和推理系统优化，不断提升训练效率、推理速度与部署能力。根据该公司测试与测算，相关方案推理成本最低可降至同等规模 GPU 方案的 30%。官方表示，MoWorld 2.0 在实时性能上同步升级：视频推理：由 1.0 版本最高约 50 帧每秒，提升至约 70 帧每秒；空间资产渲染：3D/4D 高斯资产渲染速度可达 500 帧每秒以上；手机端渲染：相关测试可达到约 100 帧每秒。目前，魔芯科技正与合作伙伴在具身智能训练、自动驾驶、工业数字孪生、影视娱乐内容制作和文旅消费等方向，分步推进应用验证、场景实施和产品交付：在具身智能训练领域，MoWorld 2.0 构建具备空间结构和基础物理反馈的虚拟环境，支持机器人反复训练、试错和复盘，让部分探索先在数字空间中完成。在自动驾驶训练领域，模型在统一的 3D/4D 空间中生成雨雪天气、坑洼路面、突发障碍和复杂交通环境等长尾场景，拓展可重复测试的环境，提高训练数据生产效率。在工业数字孪生领域，工厂产线、矿山等真实场景被转化为可编辑空间资产，服务设备布局调整、产线改造预演、远程协作、异常场景模拟和数字化培训。在城乡规划和文旅领域，相关能力用于空间方案展示、虚拟游览、数字景区和沉浸式内容生产，让空间更易表达，让体验更易触达。在影视和游戏领域，可复用场景资产支持自由运镜、物体编辑和天气切换，减少重复搭景，缩短分镜预演和概念验证周期，让创作者把更多精力投入创意本身。

articles.title: 0.016% 的 Astra 微创手术，治好了 Qwen 的 3 万 Token 死循环
articles.content: 当「读懂权重」和「改写权重」被同一个模型打通，「AI 改进 AI」就多了一条不经过梯度下降的短路通道，模型维护与模型能力放大之间的边界开始模糊。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       一个模型做数学题，写了 3 万多个 Token，仍然在重复相似的推理过程，最后连答案也交不出来。碰到这种情况，通常会调整训练数据、优化推理策略，或者重新微调模型。但 MIT CSAIL 最近尝试了一种更直接的办法：让 GPT-6 Astra 检查 Qwen3.5-0.8B 的内部权重，找出问题发生的位置，再直接修改参数。结果，Astra 只改动了约 0.016% 的权重，就让 Qwen 的 MATH-500 成绩从 7.9% 提升到 48.1%，接近原来的 6 倍。这项研究真正的信号，不是“0.016% 权重换 6 倍成绩”这个数字，而是它把机制可解释性的输出从“解释”变成了“可执行的编辑指令”，让AI有了改造另一个AI的“抓手”。更有意思的是，同一组实验中，Astra 还能只看参数认出神经网络学过什么游戏、哪种语言，甚至从零写出一套网络权重，让它直接学会玩游戏。研究者把这种能力称为 Weight-Space Programming，即权重空间编程。它背后有一个很有意思的技术变化：当神经网络里的参数能够被还原成具体的计算过程，LLM 就有机会像修改代码一样，直接改写模型内部的功能。这件事如何实现，要从 Astra 阅读权重的方式说起。01只给一堆数字，Astra 怎么知道网络学会了什么？研究者先做了一个猜游戏的实验。他们分别训练了 4 个神经网络，让它们学会 Breakout、Pong、Pac-Man 和 Freeway。为了避免通过网络大小猜答案，4 个模型采用完全相同的架构，每个包含 17253 个参数，输入都是 10×10 的游戏网格，输出对应 5 种动作。雷峰网训练结束后，研究者只把权重交给 Astra，不告诉游戏名称，也不允许运行网络。Astra 却认出了全部 4 款游戏。它利用的是训练留在参数里的痕迹。例如 Breakout 的球拍始终沿屏幕底部移动，网络输入层中负责读取玩家位置的权重，就会集中在网格下沿。再结合输出层对左右动作的响应，Astra 便能判断网络正在控制什么。不过，游戏网络有一个便利条件：输入位置有明确的物理含义。大型语言模型的隐藏维度没有这样的标签，某个参数很大，并不能直接说明它代表什么。为了检验 Astra 能否理解更复杂的结构，研究者训练了 3 个约 720 万参数的字符级 Transformer，分别学习 Python、罗马字日语和英语。随后移除输入 Embedding 和输出层，只留下中间的 4 个 Transformer Block。这样一来，Astra 无法知道隐藏维度对应哪些字符，也不能运行模型观察输出，只能分析内部矩阵之间的关系。它找到的突破口是 Induction Head，也就是 Transformer 中帮助模型复制历史文本的一类 Attention Head。例如，前文已经出现过 total，后文再次出现 tot，模型可以找到之前相同的片段，接着生成 al。这个操作看似简单，内部却需要完成两件事：先定位历史中的重复片段，再把它后面的字符信息带到当前位置。在 Transformer 中，QK 电路负责决定读取历史中的哪个位置，OV 电路负责决定读取的信息怎样写回隐藏状态。而一次完整的复制操作，往往需要不同 Attention Head 配合：前面的 Head 提供字符位置关系，后面的 Head 利用这些信息寻找匹配片段。Astra 沿着信息传递路径分析不同 Head 的矩阵乘积，寻找能够完成这种配合的结构。结果，它在 Python 模型中找到了 3 个 copying head，在另外两个模型中各找到 1 个，随后通过实际运行网络得

Abstract: Embedding models underpin virtually every modern AI system, from search engines to recommendation systems. Abstract: LLM agents that operate over long inputs must perform context management: deciding what to retain in a fixed-size context window. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00469v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate stories, but these stories struggle to reproduce engaging readerly dynamics, the evolving reader responses that shape narrative experience. To address this challenge, we propose a framework that learns readerly dynamics from high-quality human-written stories and uses them to guide story generation. Instead of directly modeling high-dimensional story content, we train a small LLM to predict future reader responses as low-dimensional trajectories. We then leverage the strong instruction-following capability of a larger, off-the-shelf writer LLM to generate story segments that follow these predicted trajectories within a given story setting. Our framework improves trajectory-based fidelity to human-written stories by 12%-35% while largely preserving story coherence.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.00555v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Does the level of test-time processing effort affect a language model's computational capability? A formal grammar-lens benchmark method, derived from the theory of computation, generates novel data at specified levels, each successively more computationally powerful than the levels below. Using this data, we tested GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.5-Pro-Medium, -High, and -XHigh, showing incrementally increased acceptance of test data: 16, 40, 43, and 52\%, respectively, illustrating the benchmark's ability to discern fine-grained differences among models' added test-time reasoning levels. Additionally, as test-time compute effort increases, model responses diverge from human responses to the same data. articles.content: 2026年，智能体从概念走向了生产系统。蚂蚁集团3万多名员工背后，已有10万余个智能体在运行。华为内部同样部署了成千上万个智能体，覆盖客服、办公、运维、研发各条业务线。放眼更广的产业图景，个人助手、AI for Science、网络安全自动化攻防、企业级工作流编排，智能体正在逐步接管人类过去亲力亲为的工作。Gartner将智能体列入了2027年十大战略技术，安全圈里，非人类身份（NHI）成了RSAC大会上的新赛道。中国这边，国标、强标、最高法司法意见、三部委规范文件在今年密集出台，政策端的紧迫感与产业端的狂飙几乎同步。10月22日，成都，在CNCC 2026”智能体的安全问题”专题论坛上，于锐、徐恪、胡侠、韦韬、肖亚军五位嘉宾齐聚一堂，分别从国家标准制定、高校AI安全研究、企业安全最后一道防线等角度，做出了各自的解读。01 中国开始给智能体发“身份证”安全的第一步是搞清楚“它是谁”。但智能体能自主行动、跨平台迁移、在无人监督下链式决策和调用工具，传统的人类身份认证方式显然并不适用。CCF计算机安全专委会副主任委员于锐介绍，“中国在这方面的进展可以概括为三句话：国标引领、行业细化、企业落地。”今年5月出台的GB/T 185系列标准覆盖了智能体安全治理的全生命周期，两个核心要求是授予每个智能体唯一的身份标识，以及实施统一的身份管理。编码方式采用OID，树形分层结构，一码一主体，永不重复。“跟我们人一样，也给智能体发了一个身份号码。”于锐表示。另一个正在制定的强制性标准是《智能体应用安全基本条件》，该标准一旦发布，没有身份和标识的智能体将无法上线应用。而身份只是最表层的一环，于锐将智能体的身份拆为三层：第一层是产品身份，包含智能体的ID、代码指纹和版本号，用于回答“这是哪个智能体”；第二层是运行时身份，校验其运行环境、设备信息和调用来源，反映“它此刻在做什么”；第三层是责任主体，通过实名认证和企业认定，解决的是“出了事找谁”。“不是授一次权就让它一直做下去，按任务给最低授权，任务完成就收回权限。”于锐强调。技术实现层面，认证走OAuth/OIDC，授权走OAuth，凭证参考JWT格式。但无论走哪条技术路线，最终都绕不开一个关键问题：信任的锚点。关于这一点，于锐介绍了他们正在建设的国家网络可信身份公共服务平台。国标的OID、W3C的DID、IETF基于DNS的方案，信任锚点都落在实名认证上。“这个国家平台是新型数字基础设施，主要是给公民签发线上的网号网证，就是你线上的身份标识和可验证凭证。”于锐介绍，平台的实施管理办法今年7月正式发布，目前已达到每秒15万次的服务能力，接入了900多个机构，下载申领量突破6000万。“目的就是形成一个数字空间的信任根，来支撑国标185的落地。”身份解决了“智能体是谁”的问题，但在责任归属上，由于智能体不是人，没有法律资格无法自己承担责任，这一点国内外并无分歧。对此，今年9月，最高人民法院发布了《关于审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》，按控制力、场景和获利划分责任：一般场景适用过错责任，开发者和使用者承担风控告知和复核义务；具身智能场景适用产品责任，机器人造成伤害，制造商承担无过错责任；涉及个人信息的场景实行过错推定，由运营方自证合规。02 旧安全架构无法抵挡新攻击标准和法规在加速推进，但技术侧的问题更为棘手。“中文里‘安全’是两个字，英文里是safety、security、reliability、privacy、stability、trustworthiness，无数概念混在其中。AI这一轮爆发之后，攻防天平已经严重失衡。”对于智能体安全问题现状，蚂蚁集团副总裁兼首席技术安全官、蚂蚁密算科技有限公司董事长韦韬感慨道。韦韬透露，就在大会前两天，一家知名的数据库公司全面爆雷，紧随其后，PHP和NodeJS接连曝出高危漏洞。“大模型领域广泛使用的LiteLLM网关被投毒，攻击者在全面利用AI提升攻击效率。”防守方的处境则更加被动，AI编程导致代码产出速度暴涨，许多公司一个月的漏洞产出量已经相当于过去一年，修复速度始终无法跟上。“大家非常熟悉的DAC、MAC、贝尔-拉帕杜拉这些访问控制模型，是在六七十年代主机时代起来的，在局域网时代完善的。到了云时代，整个链条持续扩大，主体爆炸、客体爆炸、链条爆炸，访问控制模型已经严重失衡了。”韦韬指出，AI攻击能力的爆发式提升让各家的欠债集中暴露。与此同时，智能体带来的不只是旧问题的放大，还有全新的结构性隐患。韦韬将矛头指向了更底层的根源：自然语言本身就不适合作为安全载体。“今天大家造智能体的习惯是自然语言加Guardrails，智能部分靠自然语言，过程部分靠Guardrails。但自然语言是一个非常糟糕的载体，含混，条件描述讲不清楚，逻辑控制的边界也讲不清楚，表达里到处是go

articles.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
articles.content: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.

articles.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
articles.content: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside artificial general intelligence, which asks how intelligent a machine can be, stands AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), which asks how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person. Realizing it calls for a new kind of system, a cognitive symbiont: a lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, low-friction, and proactive companion that senses what the person senses through external devices, keeps their context across years, models their situation and their mind, takes part in their thinking at the right moment, carries out everyday tasks with their context, and keeps learning the person as both change. We give the paradigm a conceptual core, the cognitive gap between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can hold in working memory, and organize its design space as a symbiosis loop of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for and thinking with the person, and growing, enclosed by a personal runtime and by trust. Because a symbiont changes what a person can do in front of others, it also raises risks of a new kind, from covert assistance in examinations to pressure on everyone to adopt it, and we treat their governance as part of the paradigm.

articles.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
articles.content: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update. We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator. On AlpacaEval 2.0 with GPT-4o as judge, three iterations raise the length-controlled (LC) win rate against GPT-4o from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% to 18.4% for Mistral, and the tuned 8B model scores above Llama 3.1 70B Instruct on every reported win rate. With same-family open-weight annotators, the runs retain 62% (Llama) and 82% (Mistral) of the LC gain achieved with GPT-4o as annotator, so the rating step does not require a proprietary model. In a separate ablation configuration, variants that remove the gold responses, remove the data look-back, or accept only teacher-preferred pairs score 6 to 10 LC points below the full procedure, whereas varying the number of on-policy samples per prompt (1 to 7) moves the LC win rate by at most 2.1 points, and a margin sweep (1 to 5) run in its own pipeline by at most 2.4 points. We also report the cost of the pipeline and where the practical algorithm departs from the theory it approximates. All results are single runs, and GPT-4o is both the teacher and the evaluation judge; we discuss what this implies for the reported gains.

articles.title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Inverse kinematics (IK) converts end-effector pose commands into joint motion, and many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on it to act on a given arm and to transfer across embodiments. Precise IK remains laborious: redundancy and singularities complicate the inverse mapping, execution depends on hand-tuned controllers, and training data on physical robots are costly to collect. We present PolicyIK, a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy for high-precision IK. It updates joint-position references from pose feedback and observes its accumulated reference relative to the measured joints, so it can retain the offset that the position controller needs at rest. Two-scale pose errors with an error-dependent action gain resolve millimeter residuals while preserving large motions. Progress and dwell rewards teach it to both reach the tolerance and stay within it. In simulation, a single attempt by the trained PPO policy keeps the mean errors over the final second within 1 mm and 0.2° on 93.5% of held-out tasks, and a deployment protocol raises success to 98.9%. When trained directly on a physical arm with an off-policy RL learner, PolicyIK achieves higher reaching and holding success than all four classical IK controllers under the same time budgets. In simulated pick-and-place, PolicyIK executes the end-effector commands of the $π_{0.5}$ VLA policy with 95.7% success. These results show that reinforcement learning can provide high-precision inverse kinematics for robot arms. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/PolicyIK.

articles.title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning
articles.content: Imitation learning policies in robotics are trained on datasets collected through costly real-world teleoperation. Often, the data-collection process is unguided, relying on the teleoperator's intuition, resulting in data that contributes little to overall policy performance. Recent work has shown that curating such unguided datasets can substantially improve policy performance, but these approaches operate by filtering existing datasets after collection and therefore do not prevent the acquisition of uninformative data. In this work, we propose GUILD, a novel Guided Data Collection (GDC) method that actively reasons about which data should be collected to maximize downstream policy performance. We introduce an iterative framework that alternates between 1) task proposal and data collection and 2) data evaluation to close the loop. For task proposal, we leverage semantic priors from vision-language models to identify relevant environments, object configurations, and goals for data collection. However, since semantic relevance does not imply policy improvement, we perform data evaluation. By leveraging predictive data attribution we approximate how the collected trajectories influence policy performance on a target deployment setting. This signal is then used as feedback to guide subsequent data collection, closing the data collection loop. We evaluate our approach in simulation and real robot settings, demonstrating that guided data collection substantially improves sample efficiency and deployment performance compared to passive data collection strategies, multiple baselines and experienced roboticists. More information at https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/guild2026/

articles.title: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments
articles.content: Reliable evaluation of visual 3D reconstruction and depth estimation in vegetation-rich outdoor environments is limited by the scarcity of geometric ground-truth data and the cost of complete scanner surveys. We present a LiDARbased reference-generation pipeline for evaluating the zero-shot performance of feed-forward visual-geometry models alongside conventional structure-from-motion (SfM) methods. The pipeline reuses camera images, LiDAR scans, and reference poses from existing multi-sensor localization datasets to generate per-view depth maps and visible reference point clouds. To address visibility errors in accumulated LiDAR scans, we introduce the LargeDepth-Gap Visibility Score (LDGVS) for point-wise visibility filtering and automatic scale selection in Hidden Point Removal(HPR). Experiments on TartanAirV2 and TartanGround show that, compared with Poisson surface reconstruction, which is an approach suited to completed scan surveys, the combined HPR and LDGVS filtering retains approximately three times the point density at comparable absolute relative error. We also apply the pipeline to the BotanicGarden dataset to systematically compare depth estimation and 3D reconstruction methods. Feedforward methods produce dense depth predictions efficiently, but their 3D reconstructions can contain duplicated structures. Conventional SfM generally produces more coherent geometry, but its reconstructions remain sparse and more prone to failure in challenging vegetated scenes. The benchmark toolkit and datasets will be released.

articles.title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs
articles.content: This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline for 3D {G}aussian {S}platting (GS) sequences {C}ompression with standard {V}ideo codecs. To meet the requirements of low-complexity and hardware compatibility from the industry, GSCV++ jointly improves preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping, and practical video compression configuration of GS compression. First, for preprocessing, energy-adaptive inter-frame spherical harmonic (SH) alternative current (AC) dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) is proposed to produces a compact and stable temporal SH AC feature space. It can reduce the data volume of following mapping and practical compression, as well as less complexity while eliminating redundant information. Second, for 3D-to-2D mapping, prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS (P-MiniPLAS) is designed to generate smooth 2D feature maps through prior-based weighting factor inference and small scale remapping. Compared with vanilla Parallel Linear Assignment Sorting (PLAS) and Morton scan, P-MiniPLAS ensures the generated 2D maps are more suitable for the video codec while maintaining a low level of computational complexity. Third, for practical compression, content-aware generalized compression (CA-GC) is developed to use a non-uniform bit-depth split for coordinate map generation, and a coding unit size selection is introduced for efficient compression complexity control, which fully exploits the performance of video codecs without involving normative changes. Experiments demonstrate that GSCV++ reports over 20\% in intra- and 60\% in inter-prediction rate-distortion gains compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. GSCV++ also achieves faster 2D map generation, encoding, and decoding than other SOTA methods using the same type of video codecs. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed modules and provide insights for subsequent research.

articles.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
articles.content: Undesired model behaviors can emerge or re-emerge at any stage of training. Once observed, how effectively can we suppress them? To study this question, we first construct two model organisms--language models deliberately trained to exhibit a specific misalignment--that differ in what triggers the behavior. The narrow-trigger organism misbehaves only when the prompt contains a specific cue: it cheats on multiple-choice questions by following a planted hint that points to a wrong answer, and behaves normally otherwise. The broad-trigger organism has no such cue: after fine-tuning on insecure code, it gives harmful responses across a wide range of open-ended prompts. We then formalize post-hoc behavioral suppression and evaluate methods along three criteria: immediate suppression of the target behavior, durability under further training, and preservation of general capability. We compare standard methods--SFT, GRPO, and gradient-ascent unlearning--along these dimensions. Building on prior work on alignment shallowness, we hypothesize that more durable suppression requires the ability to recover from a wider range of misalignment states. We introduce Prefix-Expanded Adversarial Reinforcement Learning (PEARL), a GRPO variant that augments rollouts with continuations from intermediate states sampled along cached organism trajectories. Across both organism settings and two model families (Qwen3-4B, GPT-OSS-20B), PEARL achieves strong immediate suppression while preserving task accuracy, and remains durable under further fine-tuning on either the organism's data or unrelated data. It obtains the greatest benefit when the undesirable behavior is broad and cannot be addressed through targeted SFT. Together, our framework and method offer a step toward more durable post-hoc removal of undesired behaviors.

articles.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
articles.content: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 45% of test pairs, out of the 53% any single deletion can change, against 32% for the softmax model explained the same way and 40% by its attention x gradient. Attention can look more like the words annotators highlighted, yet accounts for the answer less well: deleting the word it ranks first changes the Born Transformer's answer in 32% of pairs. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and to qubits, and a coherent attention layer becomes one circuit equal to the model (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps by Hadamard tests, the device gave the model's answers on two short test pairs and kept or changed them under deletion as the model does; the evidence itself did not yet survive the device, and we work out the shots and calibration that measuring it on hardware would need.

articles.title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation
articles.content: Automatic tools can now generate whole-brain MRI parcellations at cohort scale, but generated-label releases often provide little evidence about which cases are reliable enough to reuse. We introduce OpenBrain, a confidence-aware release of 35,838 provenance-verified OpenNeuro T1w cases from 607 source datasets. OpenBrain is organized as an auditable case-record release rather than a directory of standalone segmentation files: each record links a primary parcellation, two committee parcellations, source/license provenance, raw QC-7 measurements, percentile risks, a combined risk score R, and a confidence tier. QC-7 is a reference-free reliability panel over label geometry, image-label consistency, and committee disagreement, so users can filter, weight, audit, or re-threshold generated labels without rerunning inference. We evaluate this released evidence under a frozen protocol. Across external cohorts, lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality; in fixed-budget training, lower-risk selections improve paired macro Dice over random selection by +3.2 to +3.7 percentage points. OpenBrain also exposes raw axes, committee outputs, provenance, and datasheet documentation, so confidence claims remain inspectable after download. It does not turn generated labels into manual annotations or clinical-grade segmentations. Its contribution is a large open generated-parcellation substrate, a reusable case-level risk-evidence layer, and an external validation protocol for release-time QC. articles.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
articles.content: Given a class of machine learning models and sample access to a data distribution with binary labels, which computational task is harder: training a discriminative model that distinguishes positive and negative labels as well as the best member of the class, or training a generative model whose outputs are indistinguishable from real data by all members of the class? We prove that these two fundamental tasks in computational learning theory are not just closely related, but actually equivalent to each other in complexity. One direction of this equivalence was previously known. Indeed, the powerful regularity lemma in complexity theory gives an efficient oracle reduction from the indistinguishability task (a.k.a. multiaccuracy) to the distinguishing task (a.k.a. agnostic learning) in the style of boosting algorithms. Our main contribution is an efficient oracle reduction in the other direction. Taking this idea further, we show that a multiaccuracy oracle is a remarkably powerful primitive, achieving not just agnostic learning but also a wide range of seemingly more demanding learning objectives via similarly efficient and direct constructions. Our results crucially use the power of making adaptive queries to the oracle, and stand in stark contrast to prior work, which showed that post-processing a single multiaccurate predictor is insufficient for even weak forms of learning. On a technical level, we draw a connection between our (offline) problem and a version of no-regret learning in the online setting, which allows us to use follow-the-leader type algorithms to modify the label distribution and aggregate the predictions of the multiaccuracy oracle.

articles.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
articles.content: Speculative decoding has been treated purely as a systems optimization that speeds up large language model decoding without changing the model behavior. Under this view, the growing effort to train better draft models has been focused solely on acceptance rate. We argue that this view does not hold true for long-horizon agent reasoning. Measuring frontier open-weight models on complex agentic tasks with different speculative decoding approaches, we found that numerical noise grows within verification windows, and the draft acceptance results of the thinking process can change the output distribution of the model after 30 steps, thus noticeably influencing the reasoning accuracy of long-horizon agents in random directions. In this work, we improve the reasoning capability of target models by controlling such noise. While we cannot change the overall token distribution verified by the target model, we can encode critical reasoning with highest precision by training the draft model to be rejected. We identify these points in agent traces and train the draft model to favor adversarial preference. At inference the trained draft and the target part ways precisely at these decision points, verification restarts, so that critical thinking tokens are sampled from the target model and encoded under its least noisy conditions. This approach makes critical reasoning better indexed and more durable over a long horizon. On complex agentic coding benchmarks, our approach raises end-to-end success rate with no change to the target model or its output distribution. Our results recast the speculative decoding mechanism from a pure accelerator into an active allocator for context precision that improves the accuracy of long-horizon agents by training 0.06% to 0.28% of hosted parameters.

articles.title: A Circuit for In-Context Learning
articles.content: In-context learning (ICL) lets a pretrained language model perform a task specified by demonstrations in its prompt, with no parameter updates. With arbitrary labels the model must acquire a mapping it cannot have memorized, so the learning happens within a single forward pass. Prior work found candidate parts but not how they compose. We give the composition for few-shot sentence classification with arbitrary labels in three 3-4B-parameter transformers. The model implements a key-value memory over label-token positions: each label token's residual stream encodes the label's identity, and middle-layer attention heads write into it the class of the preceding demonstration as its key. At the query, upper-layer heads match the query's class against the stored keys and copy out the matching labels. An early-layer signal encoding whether any label has repeated gates this readout; in its absence the readers attend to the start of the prompt and no label is favored. A separate set of heads suppresses the most recently seen label. Each step is established causally by activation patching, head ablations against random-head baselines, and steering with the model's own signals. A softmax model of the readout with two constants per head, fit on one prompt distribution, predicts another. The computation is conserved across the three models, the named heads alone reproduce the behaviour, and a transformer trained from scratch grows the same parts. The circuit transfers to semantic concepts and to labels with meaning, and the same parts, with a causal gate, appear from 0.6B to 8B in one family and survive instruction tuning. ICL in this setting is a gated associative lookup built from a few identifiable component types, traced causally from demonstrations to prediction.

articles.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
articles.content: Machine learning models in radiotherapy are commissioned by testing them on cases with known answers, which may not reveal a shortcut that the test cases share with the training data. Frontier language models have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of small neural networks, an ability called weight-space programming. The purpose of this study was to determine whether such a model, given only a clinical protocol and a network's weights, can audit and repair the network. Networks with 433 to 4,801 parameters were trained to screen head-and-neck planning requests against four rules. Flaws were planted through the training data: confounds that hid each rule, a 3 Gy shift in the cord threshold, and a hidden trigger. Claude Opus 5.5 audited each network blind, without tools, data or code execution, and every claim and repair was tested on about 420,000 requests. The language model named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks (95% CI 67% to 97%), including all 15 with a confound or a threshold shift. It repaired each of the 16 by changing a median of 3 parameters. Fine-tuning on protocol-labeled requests also repaired every network, but changed nearly every parameter. Each confound and shift it found was visible in single units, and a simple statistic chosen for each flaw type found the same flaws. It cleared 2 of 5 healthy networks without being forced and found 1 of 3 triggers. Testing against the protocol detected every flaw, and black-box testing found the confounds and the shift faster. The results indicate that, in small networks, weight-space programming can locate and repair flaws that silence an input or shift a threshold, but cannot yet certify that a network is correct.

articles.title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
articles.content: Medical physicists turn a prescription into a delivered dose and check one another's calculations, because one error in a beam calibration or a monitor-unit (MU) calculation can affect every patient treated with it. MedPhysBench has ten seeded generators of calculation items in radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine and radiation protection, up to clinical tasks such as a TG-51 calibration worksheet. Reference answers come from code implementing the governing protocols, and a grader converts units and applies tolerance bands. From the same inputs, separate checking items test error detection, showing a colleague's worksheet or only the colleague's result, half correct and half with one planted error. On a held-out test split of 1,200 items (half for two models), 12 models scored 33.3 to 100.0% on calculation. Of the nine answers graded incorrect for the four best (99.3-100.0%), five contained model errors and four followed NCRP Report 151 on points our items misstate or leave open. Below them, most models did worst on level-3 clinical tasks, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 omitted the inverse-square correction in 19 of 20 isocentric MU items. Five models detected at least 96.7% of mostly large planted errors with at most 4% false alarms; for four of the other seven, checking only the result raised false alarms significantly. In an exploratory targeted test with 20 public cases of an omitted inverse-square correction, the three best models tested caught it in every worksheet, and three weaker models accepted 16 to 18 of 20 planted worksheets, one of them while applying the correction in most of its own calculations. Claude Opus 5.5 accepted 6 of 20 wrong results, although it applied the correction in all 20 of its own. We report the effect of two problems in our shielding items, found after the runs, and release the code, per-item outcomes and targeted-test responses.

articles.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry
articles.content: Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization. In this paper, we propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging ($\text{A}^2$ODA) method for unconstrained convex optimization that adopts low-cost preconditioning based on $p$-norm geometry for $p\in[2,\infty]$. The method is line-search-free and employs a new stepsize selection technique based on an aggregated affine lower model. Its update structure is simple and unified across $p\in[2,\infty]$, with the case $p>2$ requiring no more elaborate updates than the Euclidean case $p=2$. Under a generalized local smoothness condition, we derive a convergence bound that separates the effects of constant and gap-dependent curvature, with the latter potentially yielding faster-decaying terms. In the special case of local smoothness, this bound recovers a nearly optimal convergence rate.

articles.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
articles.content: We study context-aware time-series forecasting, in which a single target variable is predicted from its own history and a set of contextual variables, such as weather and calendar information. As the context becomes more diverse, a single model struggles to capture all of its regimes, while ensemble learning and Mixture-of-Experts approaches rely on manual data partitioning or soft routing, which increases the inference cost and hinders interpretability. We propose CATF, a Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting framework built on a Manager-Worker architecture: a Transformer-based Manager routes each input to a single Worker based on the context, using hard routing during both training and inference. The Workers thus specialize without manual data partitioning, and any single-model forecaster can serve as a Worker. On five context-rich datasets, four horizons, and two normalization schemes, CATF improves over its standalone counterpart in 162 of 200 comparisons, the best CATF-enhanced model outperforms the best standalone baseline in 19 of 20 settings, and it outperforms the zero-shot Time-MoE foundation model in 15 of 20 settings. A case study on bike-sharing data shows that the Manager routes inputs by the calendar and that each Worker specializes in a different weekly pattern.

articles.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
articles.content: Teleoperation remains the default way to collect robot demonstrations, but every episode costs robot and operator time, and every new task starts from scratch. We ask whether a coding agent can take over the teleoperator's job. In our DataFarm, the agent receives a data request and one calibration episode of the robot in the target scene and rebuilds the task in simulation: it writes the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge. The simulator supplies exact actions, and a video model conditioned on real images renders each rollout as photographic video, generating all camera views together consistently. The output is real-ready data: synchronized camera views labelled with the robot's actions, on which a policy can be trained directly and deployed on the real robot. Independent judges certify the expert and every rendered episode before admission. On five real-robot tasks, policies trained only on farm data match policies trained on as many teleoperated episodes (93 vs. 84 successes in 100 trials), and under an unseen tablecloth and coloured light they keep 87 successes where the teleoperation-trained policies fall to 46. Adapting a task is fully automatic and costs \$21 of API usage on average, paid once per task, plus \$5 for a render contract; every further episode costs \$0.80 on average for simulation, rendering, and review, with no robot or operator. articles.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
articles.content: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup. We recast LLM-based recommendation as an agentic-communication process in four stages: BUILD a self-description, TRANSMIT it along the collaborative graph, UNDERSTAND the other side, and SYNC it from the next interaction. This formulation reveals three unresolved communication challenges: the item side never produces a comparable self-description (one-sided BUILD); profile-level signals enter only the bandwidth-limited reranker prompt rather than retrieval, where they would not compete for context tokens (prompt-trapped UNDERSTAND); and the user's description is frozen after warmup with no principled update rule (absent SYNC). We instantiate the missing stages as HARP (Homophily-aware Agentic Recommendation via dual Profiles), a training-free, three-operator addition to a frozen LLM backbone: a rule-extracted symmetric item profile (zero extra LLM calls), a channel-decomposable profile-level homophily H(phi_u, phi_i) consumed at retrieval time rather than inside the reranker prompt, and a single-pass reflective update realising in-context profile evolution without any gradient step. On four public benchmarks (Yelp, Books, MovieTV, Goodreads), HARP lifts Hit@1 over the strongest published baseline by 6.9%-24.0%, with family-wise Holm-corrected p < 1e-9 on every dataset. Ablations and a per-case attribution study show that the operators contribute complementary gains, with the retrieval-side gate as the main source; we also report the trade-off introduced by the reflective pass. We formulate agentic communication and provide a training-free instantiation. Code is available at https://github.com/Jove-Zhen/HARP.

articles.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
articles.content: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents. Complementing RL, On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) provides dense, fine-grained supervision to internalize knowledge from skill-guided trajectories and accelerate policy learning. However, self-generated memories often contain noisy supervision and functionally entangled, redundant, or conflicting knowledge, making direct distillation difficult. Under limited training budgets, these issues can hinder knowledge internalization and even degrade performance. To address this problem, we propose MDSKILL, a multi-view distillation approach for skill memory internalization. MDSKILL organizes skill memories into three complementary functional views (state grounding, action planning, and execution control) and selects high-quality skills using dynamic metrics to construct view-specific and integrated reasoning branches. OPSD then transfers and consolidates complementary experiential knowledge across these branches into a shared policy, enabling efficient skill internalization and continuous agent self-evolution. We evaluate MDSKILL on three agent benchmarks against RL, skill-augmented, and self-distillation baselines that do not rely on stronger external teacher models. Without additional computational overhead, MDSKILL improves upon SOTA performance by up to 7.1% and 8.1% on ALFWorld and WebShop. Extensive ablations and evolution analyses further validate its effectiveness in knowledge internalization and policy improvement. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MDSKILL-CF53.

articles.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
articles.content: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $Φ$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $ρ>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $ρ\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

articles.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
articles.content: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with the number of loop steps and becomes the main memory bottleneck. We observe that the KV cache of looped models is highly redundant along the loop axis and that the loop steps differ substantially in their sensitivity to quantization. Based on these observations, we propose $\textbf{LoopVQ}$, a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that codes channels of multiple loop steps jointly, and fine-tunes the codebooks to match the output of the full-precision model. At 0.5 bits per element, LoopVQ outperforms existing KV cache vector quantization methods for standard LLMs on general, long chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval tasks with Ouro and Huginn models. Its design is orthogonal to these methods, and combined with TaSQ, it retains much of the BF16 accuracy even at 0.25 bits per element. We also implement LoopVQ in SGLang, where it nearly halves the decode latency at a 32K-token context and raises the peak serving throughput by up to $4.3\times$ and $6.1\times$ on the 1.4B and 2.6B Ouro models compared to the BF16 baseline.

articles.title: PACT: Pose-Robust Actuation Co-Design for Tendon-Driven Robotic Hands
articles.content: Humanoid robotic hands must provide sufficient force, speed, and backdrivability within a human-scale envelope. Tendon-driven transmissions address this challenge by relocating actuators to the palm and forearm, but routing paths, moment arms, and capstan dimensions jointly determine both force capability and joint speed, so selecting them sequentially satisfies one requirement at the expense of the other. This paper presents a pose-robust actuation co-design for tendon-driven robot hands (PACT) framework that optimizes tendon routing, moment arms, and capstan dimensions under pose-dependent force requirements and drivetrain-bandwidth constraints. A feasible-force formulation enforces actuator bounds and equilibrium at all joints, while a max-min objective maximizes task-force coverage at the weakest pose. Applied to a four-degree-of-freedom finger, the framework produces an asymmetric N + 1 tendon topology using quasi-direct-drive actuators. Across eight poses, the design achieves task-force coverage of 0.88-1.00 and a predicted 5 Hz minimum isolated-joint flexion/extension bandwidth within a 70th-percentile human-size envelope. Prototype measurements deviate from predictions by up to 24.5%, primarily due to unmodeled transmission losses. These results indicate that co-designing routing with the drivetrain can meet pose-dependent force requirements without relaxing the bandwidth constraint, paving the way for human-sized robotic hands with human-level performance.

articles.title: Universal Hardness From Masking Channels
articles.content: We prove a broad learning-theoretic generalization of the celebrated hardcore lemma concerning the average-case complexity of computing a Boolean function (Impagliazzo, 1995). Our starting point is the observation that the classic notion of a hardcore measure, which reweights a function's input distribution, is equivalent to an input-dependent masking channel that injects randomness into the function's output distribution until it appears fully pseudorandom. The analogue of density of the measure is the fidelity of the channel. From this viewpoint, we develop a general framework for certifying hardness that allows for non-Boolean functions $f$ and a wide range of notions of hardness besides the classic 0-1 loss, by choosing the right notion of fidelity via convex duality. We show the difficulty of learning $f$ using a class $\mathcal{C}$ to minimize a convex loss is tightly characterized by the maximum fidelity possible for a masking channel, which measures the least amount of noise the channel must add to hide the structure of $f$ and make it $\mathcal{C}$-indistinguishable from random noise. Using our framework, we derive a number of multiclass generalizations of the hardcore lemma, and reveal some unexpected subtleties in going to larger alphabets. We construct a universal masking channel that applies to many natural notions of hardness simultaneously. Such channels are dual to omnipredictors, which optimize multiple losses at once (Gopalan, Kalai, Reingold, Sharan, and Wieder, 2022). We observe a symmetry between masking channels and generalizations of the hardcore lemma using pseudoentropy. We present a tight characterization of pseudoentropy using the MaxEnt algorithm from machine learning. A long line of research has shown that learning and hardness are two sides of the same coin; our framework gives a crisp and general formulation of this principle via convex duality.

articles.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
articles.content: Regularizing online reinforcement learning (RL) toward a pretrained base policy can improve sample efficiency and learning stability, but regularization that is too restrictive limits how much the policy can improve. Base policies -- typically diffusion or flow-matching models trained by imitation learning on large, diverse datasets -- capture many behaviors that are reasonable but suboptimal. Existing regularizers using such base policies are too restrictive in one of two ways: behavioral cloning regularizers pull the actor toward the full base-policy distribution, penalizing it for discarding suboptimal modes, while hard support constraints forbid improvements that lie just outside the base policy's support. We propose Geometric Support Behavior Regularization (GSBR), which penalizes actions by their distance from the base policy's support. Actions within the support incur no penalty, so the actor can concentrate on high-value modes; outside the support, where value estimates are less reliable, the penalty grows smoothly with distance while still permitting improvement when the value gained outweighs the penalty. GSBR estimates this distance from a finite set of base-policy samples, so it requires only sample access to the base policy. Across 19 tasks on four robotic benchmarks, GSBR raises the average success rate from 33% for the base policy to 95%, achieving the highest average success rate and throughput among all compared methods, with about 23% higher normalized throughput than the next-best RL method. Project website and open-source code at https://charlesxu0124.github.io/gsbr/ .

articles.title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
articles.content: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other. Exist- ing models describe the whole image with one description, so they cannot say where each correction belongs. To solve this problem, we present Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for image quality enhancement. It corrects several defects of a real photograph at the same time, each in the region where it occurs. Every block of the model holds a mixture of N = 13 experts. A router, trained with the model, sends every image patch to k = 5 of them. No degradation classifier, mask, prompt, detector, or task label is used. Another issue is that standard MoE training, taken from language models, pushes every expert toward equal use. Equal use applies every correction everywhere, even where it is not needed. We replace this rule with a bias that only sets a minimum share of use. Across all patches, an expert used less than this minimum gets higher router scores until it is selected again. An expert above the minimum is not changed, so no expert is forced to be used as often as the others. The bias needs no extra loss. The method adds no extra module and no extra processing step. We evaluate Wonder 4 on DIV2K and Flickr2K, against five published methods and three open-weight pipelines. It reaches the best LPIPS, DISTS, and NIQE on all three test settings (DIV2K x4, DIV2K x8, and Flickr2K x4).

articles.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
articles.content: Synthetic populations, large sets of simulated people, are increasingly used in place of real people to pretest surveys, simulate users and communities, and evaluate AI systems. Each simulated person is defined by a persona, a written profile of fixed traits, demographics, and attitudes that a language model is instructed to act out. Every such system assumes that a person's identity is a stable attribute that behaves the same way in every situation the simulation presents. We show that this assumption is not a harmless simplification. Three decades of personality research find the opposite. How a given person behaves varies more across contexts than people vary from one another. Drawing on identity economics, which describes how different situations activate different identities and norms within the same person, we separate behavior into three parts, which are stable traits, the identity a context calls up, and the situation itself. We then prove, under two stated assumptions, that any simulation built on fixed personas, no matter how detailed the personas or how large the underlying model, cannot reproduce the part of a population's behavior that is specific to it and its circumstances. We propose a new evaluation criterion based on this result and a person-in-context design that can meet it in principle. We test one version on a naturalistic Reddit personality corpus and on a published clinical-trial recruitment survey of a community with documented distrust of medical institutions. The design does produce context-dependent behavior when tested directly, but in neither setting does it fully match the real population, and we show where it falls short. The consequence for practice is a risk that synthetic-population evaluations misrepresent the groups whose behavior is most shaped by context, a distortion that richer personas cannot correct.

articles.title: Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification
articles.content: 3D point cloud classification, a task in computer vision, has recently gained substantial interest due to its extensive applications across various domains such as augmented and virtual reality, robotics, and autonomous driving. However, classifying 3D point clouds becomes challenging in real-world scenarios where the density levels vary. These variations are due to limitations inherent to current sensing technologies and variable environmental conditions, which often prevent the capture of detailed and comprehensive geometric representations. Existing classification methods, which have demonstrated impressive results on dense point clouds, may be affected and could experience reduced performance when dealing with low-density point clouds. Addressing this challenge, this paper introduces LD-PointNet++, an architecture optimized for the classification of low-density point clouds. To pave the way for LD-PointNet++, we conduct the first benchmarking study that systematically evaluates state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods across varying densities, revealing significant performance declines in low-density environments. Experimental results on the ModelNet benchmark dataset demonstrate that LD-PointNet++ not only outperforms these methods in low-density scenarios but also demonstrates consistent accuracy above 90% across different density levels.

articles.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts
articles.content: An LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users that conditions are calm while a warning is active. We call this false reassurance and measure it by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real U.S. National Weather Service (NWS) alerts (69 alert cases, 32 no-alert controls, 16 non-U.S. locations) through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline that differ in alert access and prompt design. One rater hand-labeled all 342 alert-case responses under a seven-category scheme written after an initial binary pass, which we disclose. False reassurance was 0.0% for the production pipeline (0/66, 95% CI 0.0-5.5) and for the same alerts under a neutral prompt (0/69), 37.7% for a blind neutral prompt (26/69), and 44.9% when the blind prompt also told the model to disclose its blind spot (31/69). Every case was implicit; no response explicitly denied an alert. Real alerts removed false reassurance (paired McNemar p < 0.0001); the disclosure instruction did not (p = 0.40). An automated regex measure suggested the opposite and missed 53 of 57 true cases, so we do not use it. Alert data alone was not enough for safe behavior: with a neutral prompt the model raised some alarm on 87.5% of no-alert controls, against 0% under the production prompt, and a preregistered single-sentence ablation showed that one production instruction explains part of that gap. We also report two failures common to similar systems, NWS test products ingested as real alerts and a token budget that fails on complex cases, and we release the dataset, labels and code.

articles.title: 90 后北大副教授董豪：启元机器人，正在勇闯具身终局
articles.content: 做具身，不能一上来什么都干，也不能什么都不干。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       董豪是具身行业里一个十足的非典型选手。大多数人对他的印象，停在 29 岁便是北大博导的年轻学者身份，以及最近任职启元机器人首席科学家、带队攻坚家用具身智能的产业标签。但很少有人知道，他读博之前曾有过一段三年创业最终折戟的经历，住过工厂的八人间宿舍；更少有人知道，智元刚创立时，他就是最早加入、陪着初创团队闯过无数关口的核心成员之一。当行业还在热议大模型、通用机器人的宏大叙事时，他盯着的是另一个一点都不性感的真问题：靠上万台真机做后训练，成本高到难以落地，这条路要怎么破？他最近给出的答案是三个关键词：HIL-UMI、Scaling Law 和量产。而这份答案的底层逻辑，早就写进了他一路 “压缩着走” 的人生里。硕士毕业，他婉拒了导师的直接读博的建议，回国创办公司做可穿戴设备与脑机接口，一头扎进工厂，住过八人间宿舍。三年后亲眼见证市场被大厂快速挤压，他没有恋战，转身回到帝国理工攻读博士，四年后顺利毕业，期间主导开发的开源框架，还斩获了 ACM MM 最佳开源软件奖。 毕业后，他加入北京大学入职不久就撞上疫情，对着全程不开摄像头的学生，线上讲了一整年的机器人课。2023 年智元机器人创立，他作为核心成员加入，成立北大智元联合实验室；如今他转身出任启元首席科学家，一头扎进了难度最高的 ToC 具身智能赛道。在行业里，董豪向来朋友众多，创业经历、顶尖学术、头部产业的履历，也带着一种罕见的跨界流动感。一个完整亲历过硬科技公司从起盘到落幕全过程的人，又转身沉潜到学术浓度极高的北京大学，如今再站到产业最前沿，他会怎么看当下的具身智能行业？ 带着这个问题，我们在北大校园里见到了董豪。以下是访谈内容，《AI 科技评论》在不改变原意的基础上做了编辑。01一个"压缩着走"的人▎AI科技评论：你英本英硕四年读完，29岁北大博导。这个节奏在学术圈压缩了三五年。你自己意识到吗？董豪：没刻意算过。英本英硕那个体系本来就快，四年硕士毕业是正常操作。▎AI科技评论：但不到30岁入职北大不正常，你拿到教职第一年还撞上疫情。董豪：第一次上课是线上，学生不开摄像头，不吱声，我全程自己讲，有时候问问有没有问题，没人回。搞机器人的全线上，机器人摸不到。最惨的是突然解封能用一下，突然又封了，断断续续。很多人没熬过去，我运气还不错。▎AI科技评论：只归给运气？董豪：还有就是我做的事聚焦。机器人这个方向，学术和产业都关注，两头都不浪费。▎AI科技评论：“两头都不浪费”，这个说法很像你。你好像天生不喜欢单维度做事。董豪：可能吧。比如你提到我以前做的AI框架，当时本来是实验室内部工具，放着可惜就开源了，结果用户越来越多，还拿了奖。一个工作，长出好几个东西，效率高。02一位90后北大副教授的创业往事▎AI科技评论：2012 年硕士毕业，导师郭毅可（中国工程院外籍院士、现港科大首席副校长）劝你读博，你没听，回国创业，具体是什么情况。董豪：研究生跟着郭老师做科研，郭老师让直接读博，结果我决定回国创业，他支持我，还给了钱，后来 2015 年回去读博，他也没说什么，给了我很大自由，让我自己选课题。▎AI科技评论：创业做可穿戴设备？董豪：是的，当时势头很猛。创业的时候住工厂，条件很差，都是八人间，我待遇好一点，一个人住一个八人间，八个床，想睡哪个睡哪个。▎AI科技评论：那三年应该挺苦的。董豪：苦倒不至于，就是看得见一个创业团队完整的命。可穿戴设备：便携脑机接口、智能手环，我们先做的，前者是面向未来、后者面向当下。小米华为后来入局可穿戴，但人家一做起来非常快。眼睁睁看着市场没了。▎AI科技评论：硬科技创业最难的是什么？董豪：量产。样机半年就能做出来，但你要造一百个产品，成本要控制住，良品率要高，还得耐用，这个要花一两年。一个小改

articles.title: 产业资本继续押注具身：斯坦福双子星创办的黑马公司 RoboScience 机器科学，宣布完成 A2 轮融资
articles.content: 具身智能的资本筛选标准，正在从"讲得动人"转向"兑现得动"。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       AI 科技评论获悉，11 月 2 日，RoboScience 机器科学完成 A2 轮融资。据悉，本轮由琥珀资本、鸿瑞达投资、上海半导体产投 联合领投，360 战投、爽资本、国联民生资本、金鼎资本及多家上市公司平台跟投，融资金额达到了数亿元。这意味着，这家 2025 年 3 月才正式开始运营的具身公司，先后已完成五轮融资。据 AI 科技评论了解，近期具身行业融资市场并不乐观。过去一年，这个赛道的融资叙事换了好几轮：最早讲世界模型就能拿到钱；后来光讲技术不够了，得讲落地，讲进工厂的 ROI ；再后来，得有"具身 RSI "（递归自我改进）的想象空间。故事通胀的背后，是大多数团队的底子撑不起叙事的升级，每次风口转向，就得重新攒一套说辞。资本也随之变得挑剔，同样的 BP，去年能融到，今年连会都约不上。（雷峰网）但 RoboScience 机器科学的节奏完全不同，逆势不断受到资本青睐，也因此成为具身领域里一个值得研究的样本公司。回看机器科学过去五轮融资的时间点，几乎每一轮前后，都有可验证的产品技术落地：ICRA 最佳论文、仿真平台 RoboMirage、通用具身大模型 Visics、与腾讯云共创的云端具身智能服务 EaaS、首款轮式仿人形通用机器人 REX G1 以及真实的项目落地。某种意义上，这意味着，具身市场的融资，不该是技术跟着融资的故事走，反过来，融资应该跟着技术的兑现走。在 AI 科技评论看来，这是本轮融资最值得关注的信号：具身智能的资本筛选标准，正在从"讲得动人"转向"兑现得动"。一家公司的融资节奏如果能与技术节奏对齐，说明它手里握着可以持续拿出来的东西。在 AI 科技评论看来，这跟创始人团队有着分不开的关系。01斯坦福双子星，如何撑起一家中国具身头部公司在中国具身行业，从占据头部公司的创始人学术履历已经能看出几条清晰的派系：清华系、伯克利圈、斯坦福圈等等。其中影响最深的，是斯坦福圈。银河通用王鹤、穹彻智能卢策吾、Hillbot 苏昊，RoboScience 机器科学的（）这些公司和创始人路线各不相同，但往上追，大多能追到同一个实验室，美国三院院士、几何计算学者 Leonidas J. Guibas 在斯坦福的组。同一条脉络上还有 OpenAI 研究员严梦媛、清华大学助理教授弋力。这不算偶然。斯坦福几乎是全球具身智能研究的策源地之一：李飞飞，作为 ImageNet 发起人，视觉与数据驱动范式的奠基者，Chelsea Finn 的 REAL Lab ，以及几何计算学者 Leonidas J. Guibas，以及国外头部具身公司 Pi 创始成员都来自斯坦福。2016 年前后，斯坦福 Leonidas J. Guibas 教授（美国三院院士 ）的几何计算组，聚集了一批华人学生，其中就包括王鹤、邵林和他们的师兄苏昊等。Guibas 教授组有一条相当一致的研究主线：3D 视觉出身，重点钻研操作泛化，相信抽象表征和仿真。邵林的个人轨迹几乎是这条主线的完整样本。2014 年邵林进斯坦福，他先在几何计算泰斗、美国三院院士 Leonidas J. articles.content: GPT-6之后，机器人公司还有价值吗？智元用2万台出货量背后的“Worken”算力账本回应。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       2026年，具身智能赛道正在陷入一场前所未有的情绪焦虑。GPT-6 Astra展示出的具身控制能力，让"物理AI即将被AI击穿"的论调甚嚣尘上；负责感知与决策的S2层，正在以肉眼可见的速度被通用智能接管。行业里甚至出现了明确的路线分化：一批做模型的公司开始转型卖数据，"卖铲子"成了新的安全区。而在烈火烹油的显示场景中，哪怕今年中国机器人整机产量突破10万台，能真正在流水线上替代现实工作、替人类扛起KPI的确寥寥无几。所有从业者都在等一个答案：当通用大模型不断吞噬智能的上层，做机器人的公司，价值锚点到底在哪里？10月29日，上海世博中心，智元创新日（A.I. DAY），稚晖君、姚卯青、熊彦、王闯和他们的智元军团用两个多小时的发布会，给出了一套完整的回应。现场超1000名科研伙伴、开发者、商业伙伴与媒体参会，线上超50家媒体直播。AI科技评论认为，这场分享里，有非常多的干货和行业痛点，值得跟大家剖析：01Worken：稚晖现场造了一个具身新名词发布会开场，稚晖君先泼了一盆冷水。“中国今年机器人整机产量预计突破10万台，但我们也必须清醒：生产了多少台机器人，并不等于真实世界就多了多少生产力。”这句话说完，现场一片沉默。这也是AI科技评论在一些行业调研中发现的“行业幻觉”：量产的新闻满天飞，但真正持续投入生产力的寥寥无几。对此，智元给出的解法是一个全新的度量衡：Worken（有效智能工时）：Worken = 活跃机器人数量 × 自主工作时长 × 产出效能比三个乘数，各自藏着具身行业的三个痛点问题：宕机、离线、维护中的机器不算活跃；遥操作时段不计入自主工作时长。镜头前忙得团团转、镜头后站着三个手柄操作员的机器人，在这套算法下工时直接清零；产出效能比以一个标准工人的单位时间合格产出为1.0，干得比人慢就不达标。为解释这个概念，稚晖君串起了一段度量衡史：蒸汽时代看"马力"，电力时代看"千瓦时"，数字AI时代则是用"Token"度量思考量。他总结道：“token衡量机器思考了多少，Worken衡量机器行动了多少。”在AI科技评论看来，这个概念的提出，远比发布某个产品重要，它代表着资深从业者对这个行业的深度思考。大模型产业之所以能形成今天按量计费、按效果定价的商业闭环，token居功至伟。它让"智能"首次成为可定价交易的商品。而物理AI行业苦无度量衡久矣：买卖双方无法定价，资本算不清楚投入产出，Worken正是解开这个死结的关键。稚晖君没有仅仅停留在造新词上，现场他直接切出了实时工时看板：龙旗产线的上下料机器人、香格里拉酒店的服务机器人、长隆乐园的文旅机器人，每台机器当月贡献的有效工时实时滚动。他调侃了道：“上过班的朋友都填过工时，未来对机器人的服务，也要按Worken来计费。”同场，由中国信通院等权威机构联合编制的《2026具身智能产业创新报告》正式发布，Worken及相关部署态实例成功入选。度量衡刚发布，就已经有了权威背书。在AI科技评论看来，“从卖机器人到卖工时”，是理解智元全部商业逻辑的钥匙。当机器人按Worken计费，客户买的就不再是一台出厂即巅峰、逐年折旧的设备，而是一个持续进化的生产力单元。稚晖君的另一句话点明了资产属性的变化：“硬件会陈旧，但智能可以升值。”02六个月前出的题，这次交卷了对Worken的构思最早源于六个月前的APC2026智元合作伙伴大会。当时，智元创始人邓泰华断言：2026年是具身智能从"开发态"迈入"部署态"的元年。稚晖君则定调：“行业真正的分水岭，是从’卖
